source.note: Plan row 200 (Quaternius static Round shield via poly.pizza) is blocked, so this is Shield_Round_2.fbx from Quaternius's own CC0 Medieval Weapons Pack on OpenGameArt (same author, licence on the page; the same zip and pin as the sword and axe entries). The pack has two round shields with the same mesh: Shield_Round (plain wood planks) and Shield_Round_2 (the same planks quartered with white paint); Shield_Celtic_Golden was rendered too but is a tall waisted gold-and-gem shield, not round. Shield_Round_2 was taken because the quartered face reads as a shield at a glance in cel, where plain planks become one amber disc. Height 0.7 m is the diameter (a typical 0.6-0.9 m round shield). Rest pose: upright, painted face toward +Z, bottom rim on y = 0, centred on x = 0; a 14-sided steel rim with 8 rivets around a shallow plank dome (front of the dome at z about +0.10 m, board back at z about -0.03 m). Grip: two short vertical wooden handles on the back (-Z side), at x about -0.14 and +0.14 m, from y about 0.25 to 0.49 m, standing out to z about -0.12 m; the shield's centre is at y 0.35 m. To put it on an arm: parent to the forearm/hand so the arm passes through both handles along X (or hold one handle in the fist), with +Z (the face) pointing away from the body. Colours match the sword and axe: rim and rivets pale steel (moon over sky), wood planks amber over sky; the source's white paint is mapped to the script's red accent (paint), since white paint against the pale steel rim lost the quartering. Wood and paint thresholds are 0 so the gently domed face stays lit in the front views.
